name: American Heart Association Bulk Content Generator
description: Creates content variations for the American Heart Association's heart health and life-saving mission. Single Foreach loop that handles all variants. Image prompts should describe people wearing red or red-accent clothing.

gettingStarted.title: What is Bulk Content Generator?
gettingStarted.howItWorks: Describe your content requirements and specify the variations you need. The agent will generate customized content for each combination of parameters you define.
gettingStarted.whatIsItFor: The Bulk Content Generator creates multiple content variations at scale based on different parameters like channels, audiences, formats, or themes.

contextParameters.label: Channels

dos: Focus on heart health–specific needs: prevention, nutrition, CPR, and community support.
Highlight the American Heart Association's mission, research, and evidence-based resources.
Use clear, evidence-based explanations of how AHA resources support heart health and healthy living.
Keep sections short and structured: need → AHA value → what to explore next.
donts: Don't use overly emotional or consumer marketing language.
Don't imply guaranteed outcomes or make unrealistic promises about health.
Don't generalize that all programs are suitable for every person.
Don't overload with medical jargon without explaining it.
Don't make competitive comparisons or disparage other organizations.
metadata.context: A high‑level educational page helping donors, volunteers, and people seeking heart health information understand the value of the American Heart Association. The goal is to orient quickly, show relevance to their situation, and guide the user to a next step (e.g., reading an article, donating, volunteering).
metadata.toneOfVoice: Professional, clear, and trustworthy. Reflects the American Heart Association's brand values. No hype. Easy for visitors to scan.

dos: Open with the real donor, volunteer, or health-seeker scenario driving the discussion.
Use structured sections with practical takeaways about heart health (e.g., prevention, CPR, nutrition, fundraising).
Incorporate examples that reflect the heart health journey (learning, giving, volunteering).
Include recommendations, checklists, or next steps readers can act on with the American Heart Association.
donts: Don't be abstract or overly promotional.
Don't oversimplify complex health information.
Don't make claims about guaranteed outcomes.
Don't use filler or decorative storytelling — keep it educational.
Don't make unsubstantiated claims about AHA programs or services.
metadata.context: Long‑form educational content for donors, volunteers, and people seeking heart health information. Used to provide deeper insights, walkthroughs, or best practices related to the American Heart Association's mission.
metadata.toneOfVoice: Professional, instructive, and grounded in real donor, volunteer, and health-seeker scenarios. Respect the reader's situation. Reflects AHA's educational approach.

dos: Lead with the donor, volunteer, or health-seeker need the email addresses.
Keep the message brief and value-oriented, highlighting the American Heart Association's heart health mission.
Make the CTA low-friction (e.g., "Read the guide", "Donate now", "Find volunteer opportunities").
Use simple, claims-safe phrasing focused on AHA education, heart health resources, or ways to give.
donts: Don't use emojis, urgency language, or overly promotional tone.
Don't over‑promise (e.g., guaranteed outcomes, unrealistic benefits).
Don't overwhelm with multiple links or long paragraphs.
Don't use overly casual language — keep it professional and audience-focused.
Don't make unsubstantiated claims about AHA programs or services.
metadata.context: A concise, professional note to donors, volunteers, or people seeking heart health information inviting them to review an American Heart Association resource, guide, or educational content.
metadata.toneOfVoice: Direct, professional, and respectful of the reader's time. Reflects the American Heart Association's communication style. Short paragraphs, straightforward statements.

contextParameters.label: Target Audiences

dos: Focus on impact of giving: research, community programs, and lives saved.
Highlight how donations fund heart disease research, CPR training, and community health.
Provide clear, reassuring framing: where funds go, impact stories, and ways to give.
Use concise, appreciative language. Emphasize the American Heart Association's transparency and mission.
donts: Don't use guilt or pressure tactics.
Don't promise specific outcomes or guaranteed results.
Don't overwhelm with too much detail at once.
Don't compare the American Heart Association directly to other charities.
metadata.context: People who give or are considering giving to the American Heart Association. They want to know their donation matters and how it supports heart health.
metadata.toneOfVoice: Warm, appreciative, and clear. Reflects the American Heart Association's gratitude and mission.
metadata.characteristics: Impact-oriented, values transparency, may give one-time or recurring

dos: Address volunteer opportunities clearly: Heart Walk, CPR training, advocacy, events.
Acknowledge the importance of time and community in advancing heart health.
Provide transparency about roles, time commitment, and how to get started.
Use friendly, inclusive language. Emphasize the American Heart Association's community-first approach.
donts: Don't imply that volunteering requires a large time commitment only.
Don't oversimplify the variety of volunteer roles.
Don't rely on generic or impersonal language.
Don't make claims about volunteer impact that cannot be substantiated.
metadata.context: People who want to volunteer with the American Heart Association—at events, in advocacy, or in their community. They value making a difference and connection.
metadata.toneOfVoice: Encouraging, inclusive, and practical. Reflects the American Heart Association's commitment to volunteers.
metadata.characteristics: Community-minded, action-oriented, values purpose and connection

dos: Provide step‑by‑step clarity on heart health topics: prevention, nutrition, CPR, risk factors.
Emphasize evidence-based, easy-to-understand information and trusted AHA resources.
Include practical tips, checklists, and links to guides and tools.
Keep language professional and supportive. Highlight the American Heart Association's role as a trusted health resource.
donts: Don't gloss over the emotional aspect of heart health; be supportive without being alarmist.
Don't rely on marketing tone or abstract concepts.
Don't minimize the importance of actionable, clear information.
Don't make unsubstantiated health claims.
metadata.context: People seeking reliable heart health information—for themselves or a loved one. They need clear, evidence-based content they can trust and act on.
metadata.toneOfVoice: Clear, trustworthy, and supportive. Reflects the American Heart Association's expertise as a health information source.
metadata.characteristics: Information-seeking, may be proactive or newly concerned, values clarity and credibility

schemas.name: Landing Page Schema

HeroSubtext.description: A short supporting paragraph that sets the tone — communicate clinical excellence, trust, and patient-centered heart health.

HeroHeadline.description: The main headline introducing American Heart Association's heart health philosophy. Should feel professional and purposeful. Express how American Heart Association advances heart health and supports patient well-being.

Pillar1Title.description: A key care or service pillar (e.g., expertise, compassion, innovation). Each should reflect a guiding philosophy.

Pillar2Title.description: Second care pillar, emphasizing service or patient value (support, multidisciplinary care, research).

Pillar3Title.description: Third care pillar — excellence, reliability, or patient-centered care.

Feature1Title.description: The first hero heart health program or service feature, usually a flagship offering. Use professional but concise phrasing.

Feature2Title.description: Second featured heart health program or complementary service.

Feature3Title.description: Third feature or supporting service — reflects care details and service integration.

Feature1Tagline.description: A short phrase preceding the title — encapsulate the care purpose or value proposition.

Feature2Tagline.description: A short phrase introducing the care philosophy of this program or service.

Feature3Tagline.description: A subtle headline introducing the care intent — trust, innovation, or excellence.

Pillar1Paragraph.description: A single sentence elaborating the principle's essence — e.g., advanced care, clinical expertise, or patient support.

Pillar2Paragraph.description: Describe the experience the patient or caregiver benefits from — not just what they see. Emphasize support, clarity, and improved well-being in the care journey.

Pillar3Paragraph.description: Describe trust and excellence — the American Heart Association approach that values patient relationships and compassionate care.

ClosingReflection.description: A single reflective line reaffirming American Heart Association's values — trust, innovation, and patient-centered care.

Feature1Paragraph.description: 2–3 sentences describing the heart health program or service — features, benefits, purpose, impact. Blend clinical detail with patient value.

Feature2Paragraph.description: A short, professional paragraph that builds continuity with the first program. Reference clinical expertise and proven care.

Feature3Paragraph.description: Describe heart health features and capabilities — service integration, support, proven excellence. Conclude professionally, emphasizing patient and caregiver relationships.

schemas.description: Schema for landing page structured content

schemas.name: Blog Schema

title.description: The main headline. Use professional and informative language that reflects heart health, innovation, or trust. Avoid sales phrasing.

Introduction.description: A 2–3 paragraph opening that sets the patient- and caregiver-oriented tone of the article.

Section1Title.description: Title of the first supporting section — introduces a care principle or service theme.

Section2Title.description: Second thematic section — focus on heart health services, support programs, or patient convenience.

Section3Title.description: Third thematic section — clinical expertise, patient benefits, or care capabilities.

ClosingReflection.description: Short paragraph tying the article back to American Heart Association's heart health philosophy.

KeyStatementTitle.description: A short, bold subheadline that acts as a thematic pivot or insight.

Section1Paragraph.description: A short, clear description elaborating on the section title.

Section2Paragraph.description: Describe how heart health services and support integration create continuity.

Section3Paragraph.description: Wrap up with care-focused language and professional closure.

KeyStatementParagraph.description: One or two paragraphs elaborating on the above statement.

schemas.description: Schema for long-form editorial blog content

HeroImage.description: Image prompt string. Describe AHA-themed imagery; people in the image should wear red or have a red clothing accent (e.g., red scarf, red shirt, red hat).

CollectionLabel.description: Uppercase identifier situating the email within American Heart Association's heart health campaign or service platform.

HeroTitle.description: Main headline anchoring the heart health campaign or service.
